statement: 2. Improved student coping mechanisms

statement: exchange healthy coping mechanisms

statement: Participants strengthen comfort with challenge
why: Comfort with challenge reads as a belief that one can handle hard things, the Y5.4 side of resilience.

statement: Youth will believe they can handle hard situations on their own.
why: States a general belief in handling challenges with no coping skill named, which the tie-breaker sends to Y5.4.

statement: build student resilience
why: Bare resilience with no coping skill or belief named; this is the case the hint must settle (P votes Y4.2).

statement: build resilience
why: A second bare resilience target, from a therapeutic songwriting program, to test the same open default.

statement: 3 Girls gain practical life skills.
why: Practical life skills with no skill named, the bare case the proposed Y7.7 include would cover.

statement: learn life skills that will help them prepare for adulthood
why: Life skills tied to preparing for adulthood, which fits Y7.7 independent living.

side: the named skill's own code (not Y7.7)
statement: learn key life skills such as team work

side: the named skill's own code (not Y7.7)
statement: Students will build life skills such as budgeting and managing their own money.
why: Money-only skills are excluded from Y7.7, so this should go to Y7.6 even though it says life skills.

statement: 3. Proficiency in basic business planning and market research.
why: Business planning and market research are technical business skills, the business-creation side (Y7.4).

statement: Teens will launch a small business and make their first sales.
why: Starting a business is the business-creation case that batch 1 routes to Y7.4.

statement: Students will pitch their business idea to a panel of community judges.
why: Pitching is speaking to an audience, so it should go to Y4.6 even inside an entrepreneurship program.

statement: Youth will present a clear, persuasive product pitch to local investors.
why: A second pitching row, where the result is presentation skill and not the business itself.

statement: 1. Mastery of the fundamentals of the entrepreneurial mindset (risk-taking, initiative).
why: An entrepreneurial mindset of risk-taking and initiative has no settled home; the live run gave it Y5.6.

statement: Students will develop an entrepreneurial mindset.
why: A bare mindset row with no skill named, to test whether it goes to Y5.6, Y7.4 or Y7 domain-only.

statement: Students gain greater self awareness
why: Bare self-awareness that names neither emotions nor identity, the case proposed for Y4 domain-only.

statement: increase self-awareness
why: A second bare self-awareness target; the live run split such texts between Y4.1 and Y5.1.

statement: identify and address their emotions
why: Identifying one's emotions is Y4.1 emotion awareness (the "address" half may also pull Y4.2).

statement: Students will recognize and name their feelings when they are upset.
why: Naming one's own feelings is the Y4.1 core, so bare self-awareness rules must not pull it away.

statement: inspire self-discovery
why: Self-discovery is about understanding who one is, the Y5.1 side.

statement: Youth will explore their identity and describe what matters most to them.
why: Identity exploration and naming one's values are Y5.1, not emotion awareness.

statement: Long-term: Underserved public schools successfully close the art-education gap, creating equitable access to creative growth and permanently integrating diverse cultural narratives within the broader School District.
why: A school district permanently building cultural content into its arts teaching is an institution adopting a practice (compound statement).

statement: Each partner school will adopt the garden curriculum as part of its regular science block.
why: A school formally adopting a program into its curriculum, the practice case A3.1 option (a) would cover.

statement: improving school culture
why: School culture improving with no formal adoption of a policy, program or practice named, so it should not reach A3.1.

statement: ignite a college-going culture in their schools
why: A college-going culture in schools is a school-wide condition, not a formal adoption, so A3 domain-only.

statement: Older adult tutors will gain skills in phonics-based reading support.

statement: Bigs live with a sense of satisfaction in positively contributing to their Little’s development
why: Volunteers' satisfaction with serving is the A1.3 side of the volunteer routing rule.

statement: Volunteer tutors will return to serve for a second school year.
why: Volunteer retention in the role is A1.3 under the routing rule.

statement: Increased number of tutors remaining in the education field after service

statement: Older adult volunteers will feel less isolated and report better well-being from tutoring.
why: Senior volunteers' own quality of life is A1 domain-only under the chosen rule; the rejected option sent it to A1.3.

statement: The program will fill all open youth worker positions before summer camp begins.

statement: Each site coordinator will earn a youth development credential.
why: One person earning a credential is A1.1 under the tie-breaker, not a staffing level.

statement: Our lead counselor will complete certification in trauma-informed care.

why: Students' own fruit and vegetable intake is Y8.1 even though "at home" is named.

statement: Increased student preference for healthy food choices as aligned with Dietary Guidelines.

statement: Families will cook healthy meals together at home at least three times a week.
why: The household's eating practice changes, so F1.3 under the whose-eating rule.

statement: Caregivers will pack more fruits and vegetables in their children's lunches.

statement: Documented prevention of youth entry into the formal child welfare system.

statement: Young people placed out of home will rebuild trust with their parents.
why: The young person's own family relationship stays Y3.4 when the setting is child welfare.
